jobs.name: 地图01_近岸小环线
jobs.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: practical, SIMPLE, true TOP-DOWN TERRAIN BLOCKOUT AND PLAYER-GUIDANCE PLAN for a small cozy third-person game "Weather House".
Reference roles: Image 1 (A3 concept painting) establishes that the cottage DIRECTLY ADJOINS the pond bank. Image 2 (B2) establishes a nearby old-tree courtyard with a drying rack, frog moss bed and shared clear ground. Image 3 (C1) establishes another accessible animal-interaction bank on the SAME pond, not a separate water body. Image 4 (D2) establishes a modest hill where one sees the cottage to the left of the pond in the same view. These references constrain adjacency, scale relationships and viewpoints; do not imitate their perspective or painting detail.
ONE square map, overhead ground-plan projection, north at top by convention. Flat diagram on warm off-white ground. This is a schematic for building terrain, not a decorative illustrated adventure map. Simple filled polygons, thin clear lines, lots of negative space. Roofs are footprint rectangles, old tree is one irregular canopy symbol, woods are a few connected flat dark-sage masses with no individually rendered leaves. Light sage open grass, pale blue ONE pond, pale beige activity clearings, muted ochre hill with only three thin contour lines. A few gray rock footprints. No illustrated facades, no 3D perspective, no relief rendering, no realistic shadows, no watercolor texture, no hundreds of trees, no grass or flowers.
LOCKED SPATIAL RELATIONSHIPS IN ALL OPTIONS:
- One cottage A on the WEST BANK of the one pond. Rough map coordinates: cottage center 30% from left and 62% from top; its east wall ends around 35% width; the pond's west bank begins around 39% width. ONLY a narrow yard/shore strip less than half a cottage width separates the wall from the water. No forest belt, broad road, broad lawn or separate district between house and water. The house MUST visibly touch the shoreline neighborhood. A tiny bank path and waterside stepping stones recall reference A3.
- One pond centered around 58% width and 55% height; irregular roughly oval water extends about 39–77% width and 33–76% height. No second pond. A is on its southwest/west shore. C is an ANIMAL-ACTIVITY CLEARING ON THE NORTH / NORTHEAST BANK OF THIS SAME POND, not the pond itself relocated elsewhere.
- B, old-tree teaching courtyard, is immediately northwest of A, near 23% width and 34% height. A short path connects the house entrance to B and the old tree is visible as a landmark from the entrance. Within the one B clearing, a small twig rack and a small moss-bed oval sit on opposite sides of ONE shared walkable space only a few steps apart; not two distant arenas. Tiny frog/squirrel icons are not required.
- D is a modest grassy ridge or hill at the SOUTHEAST, around 84% width and 82% height. A broad gradual approach follows the east bank from C toward D, and a shorter return hugs the southern bank back to A. At the crest looking northwest the house is on the left and the pond on the right, matching reference D2. Reserve an OPEN VIEW CORRIDOR from D across the pond toward A; no tall woodland wall in this sightline.
PLAYER GUIDANCE TO SHOW SPATIALLY:
A porch -> short old-tree landmark path -> B compact learning courtyard -> a framed opening onto the north pond bank -> C activity clearing -> curving east-bank climb -> D crest reveal -> shoreline return to A. A and C are two experiences around the SAME water. B has one readable onward opening; small woodland edges give directed framing but no hard gates. A simple bird perch near B's exit and a low rock/deer waiting spot at the foot of the D climb may be tiny plain symbols. Conceal some of the wide view along the uphill approach using a small tree mass beside the path, but open the vista at D. The return comes back beside the repaired B/A home cluster so the earlier change can be noticed.
GRAPHIC OVERLAY:
One clean bold label A by cottage, B inside courtyard, C at the northern activity shore, D at hill crest. Exactly one of each. Broad continuous beige routes on traversable ground. Overlay a few SMALL muted-orange directional arrowheads for the first-visit route A->B->C->D, and a few muted-purple arrowheads for the short D->A shoreline return. Two thin dashed blue sightlines from D terminate at the cottage and pond, showing the home-and-water overlook; make the lines secondary and unobtrusive. Do not draw paths through water. Hill access is a gently curving path, not stairs or sheer cliffs.
No other text or numbers, no title, no legend, no compass rose, no border, no UI. Labels and arrows must not cover landmarks. Keep the shoreline adjacency obvious even at thumbnail scale. Entire layout small and walkable; one cottage only.
OPTION 1 — BASELINE SHORE LOOP: Follow the locked arrangement closely. B is an open but sheltered courtyard. A->B is the shortest leg, B->C a gentle curve along the northwest pond rim, C->D follows the eastern shore uphill, D->A follows the southern shore home. Keep the pond visually dominant enough to connect the areas, but not oversized. A's short bank apron faces the water. The main differentiator is maximum clarity, a compact learning zone and a single legible scenic loop. Only 6–8 broad woodland patches total. Render about 30–40 simple graphic shapes total, not a dense forest illustration.
